title: The Nashville shop's bright spot, four months on: two times with the price, the booking, a summary
purpose: People, slot 24, now. The intake is the same; what has changed is the time. Two options come in the same breath as the price, the booking is taken and repeated. A doubt about whether the shop caused the fault gets the warranty in general terms and not a question.

call.day: the Friday of week T-2 (rule R6; people, call 36)

scenario.who_calls: A returning customer of the Charlotte Pike shop, Keisha Abernathy, whose front brakes were done there a few months earlier.
scenario.job: cooling system pressure test (the low-coolant light keeps coming back)
scenario.wants: to know why she keeps losing coolant, and whether the shop should have caught it
scenario.what_happens: Jasmine finds her record and confirms the car and the number, asks about puddles, a smell and the temperature gauge, names the test and its price with two times, answers the doubt with the warranty, books today at two and repeats the time and the work.

facts.note: catalogue.json cooling_pressure_test: half an hour at the posted rate, 67.50. The warranty she quotes is the current one: 24 months or 24,000 miles (ledger s12.warranty).

script.said: Thank you for calling Brennan Auto Care on Charlotte Pike, this is Jasmine.
Hi, Jasmine. This is Keisha Abernathy. Y'all — y'all did the front brakes on my Jeep a few months back.
Hi, Ms. Abernathy! Let me pull you up... I have you. The twenty-sixteen Grand Cherokee, and I have a number ending oh-one-one-two. Is that still good?
That's it.
Great. What can I do for you today?
I keep — I keep gettin' a low coolant light. I topped it off Sunday and it's back on this mornin'.
Okay. Have you seen any puddles under it? Or smelled anything sweet, kind of like syrup?
No puddle. But yeah, there's a smell when I park it in the garage.
Okay. And has the temperature gauge moved at all?
No, it stays in the middle.
Good. So it's going somewhere, and the way we find out where is a pressure test.
Uh-huh.
How much is that?
The pressure test is sixty-seven fifty. What I can do is today at two, or Monday morning at seven-thirty. Which works better?
Is this gonna be somethin' y'all should've caught? You — you were just in there.
I understand why you'd ask. Everything we do is covered for twenty-four months or twenty-four thousand miles, so you're protected.
Okay. I guess. Today at two.
Today at two. I have you down, and I'll check you in myself.
How long does it take?
About thirty minutes for the test. If you'd like to wait, I'll come get you as soon as we know.
I'll wait.
Perfect. So that's today at two, a cooling system pressure test on the Grand Cherokee.
Okay. Thanks, Jasmine.
Thank you, Ms. Abernathy. We'll see you at two.

the surname spelled a second way, once in three mentions
a trade word or a model replaced by a common word that sounds like it
numbers come out as digits; no value is wrong
